mainEntity.name: How long do dentures typically last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Conventional acrylic dentures typically last between five and ten years with proper care, though this varies depending on wear, oral changes, and maintenance. Over time, as the shape of the jawbone changes, dentures may become loose or uncomfortable and may need to be relined or replaced. Regular dental reviews help ensure your dentures continue to fit well. Implant components may have a different lifespan and your dentist will advise on this individually.

mainEntity.name: Can I sleep with my dentures in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most dentists recommend removing conventional dentures at night to allow gum tissue to rest and to help prevent bacterial build-up beneath the denture. However, guidance may differ for implant-retained prosthetics. Always follow the specific advice given by your own dental professional, as individual circumstances can influence this recommendation.

mainEntity.name: Are dentures noticeable to other people?

acceptedAnswer.text: Modern dentures are designed to look natural and are customised to match your facial features, skin tone, and preferred tooth appearance. Advances in dental materials and manufacturing mean that well-fitted, professionally made dentures are generally not conspicuous. Poorly fitting or older dentures may appear less natural, which is another reason why regular review and timely replacement or adjustment is worthwhile.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between implant-retained dentures and a dental implant bridge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Implant-retained dentures are typically removable prosthetics that clip onto implants placed in the jawbone, providing improved stability compared to conventional dentures. A dental implant bridge is a fixed restoration supported by implants that is permanently attached and cannot be removed by the patient. Both options offer greater stability than conventional dentures, but they differ in design, cost, maintenance, and clinical suitability. Your dentist will assess which approach is appropriate based on your bone health and clinical presentation.

mainEntity.name: Will dentures affect what I can eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: An adjustment period is expected with any new dentures, particularly regarding chewing. Most patients gradually adapt to eating a wide range of foods comfortably, though very hard or sticky foods may need to be approached with care. Implant-retained dentures generally allow for more confident chewing than conventional removable dentures. Your dental team can provide guidance specific to your type of denture.

mainEntity.name: How much do dentures cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Denture costs in the UK vary considerably depending on the type (full, partial, flexible, or implant-retained), the materials used, and the dental practice. NHS dentures are available at a standard charge, while private dentures offer a wider choice of materials and aesthetics. Implant-retained dentures involve a higher investment due to the implant surgery and prosthetic components involved. It is advisable to request a clear written treatment plan and cost breakdown before proceeding.
